title: CRLA/178/2010 of YOGESH @ YOGI AND ANR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No. 178 of 2010
Yogesh and another. ÖÖ.Appellants.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand. .....Ö. Respondent.
Present:
Mr. Narayan Har Gupta, Amicus Curiae for the appellants.
Mr. S.K. Chaudhary, Addl. GA for the State.
Honíble Alok Singh, J (Oral).
None was present on behalf of appellants, so Mr.
Narayan Har Gupta, Advocate, present in the Court, was
requested to assist the Court on behalf of appellants. He
accepted request of this Court. Therefore, Mr. Narayan Har
Gupta, was appointed as Amicus Curiae on behalf of appellants
in pre lunch session and paper book was handed over to him
and he argued the appeal in post lunch session.
Present appeal is directed against the judgment and
order dated 17.07.2010 passed by Special Judge, Gangster Act /
1st Additional Sessions Judge, Haridwar in Special Sessions
Trial No. 03 of 2003 whereby appellants were held guilty for the
offence punishable under Section 2/3 of the U.P. Gangsters and
Anti Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986 (for short ìthe
Gangster Actî) and were sentenced to undergo 2 years rigorous
imprisonment each and to pay fine of ` 5,000/- each and in
default of making payment of fine, to undergo additional
rigorous imprisonment of two month.
Brief facts of the present case, inter alia, are that an
FIR was got registered against appellants and two other
persons namely Neeraj and Ramnath under Section 2/3 of the

2
Gangsters Act, after obtaining consent from the Collector,
Haridwar and Senior Superintendent of Police, Haridwar
stating therein that appellants and two others constituted a
gang of criminals and were involved in various offences
provided under Chapter 16, 17, 22 of the Indian Penal Code;
people are afraid of them and nobody was ready to report
against them due to their fear; following cases were shown to
have been registered against appellant Yogesh:
i. Case Crime No. 189/97 under Section 307 IPC
police station Laksar, Haridwar.
ii. Case Crime No. 40/96 under Section 307, 506 IPC
police station Laksar, Haridwar.
iii. Case Crime No. 182/98 under Section 389, 304
IPC police station Laksar, Haridwar.
iv. Case Crime No. 94/95 under Section 323, 325 IPC
police station Laksar, Haridwar.
v. Case Crime No. 87/99 under Section 380, 411 IPC
police station Laksar, Haridwar.
vi. Case Crime No. 213/99 under Section 504, 506
IPC police station Laksar, Haridwar.
vii. Case Crime No. 7/2000 under Section 18/20 of the
NDPS Act, police station Laksar, Haridwar.
viii. Case Crime No. 197/2001 under Section 3 of the
Gunda Act police station Laksar, Haridwar.
ix. Case Crime No. 272/2001 under Section 302 IPC
police station Laksar, Haridwar.

3
x. Case Crime No. 284/2001 under Section 25 Arms
Act police station Laksar, Haridwar.
xi. Case Crime No. 278/2001 under Section 25 Arms
Act police station Laksar, Haridwar.
 Following cases were shown to have been
registered against the appellant Moni:
i. Case Crime No. 87/99 under Section 380, 411 IPC police
station Laksar, Haridwar.
ii. Case Crime No. 213/99 under Section 504, 506 IPC
police station Laksar, Haridwar.
iii. Case Crime No. 272/2001 under Section 302 IPC police
station Laksar, Haridwar.
iv. Case Crime No. 278/2001 under Section 25 Arms Act
police station Laksar, Haridwar.
To prove the prosecution story PW1 Darban Singh,
PW2 Sushil Kumar, PW3 SI Rajveer Singh, PW4 Mandhata
Samrat, PW5 Ved Prakash, PW6 Rakam Singh were examined.
Thereafter, statements of appellants were also recorded under
Section 313 Cr.P.C.
PW1 Darbhan Singh stated, on oath, that in the year
2002, he was posted as SO, police station Laksar and he
prepared gang-charts against appellants whereupon consent
was obtained from the Collector; appellants and two others had
formed a gang of criminals and were involved in serious
offences like loot, dacoity, theft and murder; people were afraid
of them and none could dare to come out to depose against

4
them because of their fear. PW1 Darban Singh proved the gang-chart prepared by him against the appellants.
PW5 Ved Prakash stated, on oath, that on
24.11.2001, appellant no. 1 Yogesh came his house, when his
brother Om Prakash had gone to his shop, he started teasing
and molesting wife of Om Prakash; wife of Om Prakash
narrated the entire incident to Om Prakash; Om Prakash went
to the house of appellant and narrated the entire incident to his
father; in the evening when Om Prakash was in his home,
appellants along with Neeraj and Ram Nath came to his house
and asked for Om Prakash; Om Prakash, Ved Prakash (PW5),
Gulab Singh, Lakhan Singh came out together; the moment
they came out, Yogesh shot at Om Prakash while Moni
assaulted him with knife; when Gulab Singh tried to intervene,
he was also assaulted by Yogesh and Moni; Om Prakash died
on the spot, thereafter, FIR of Case Crime No. 272 of 2001 under
Section 302, 307 IPC was got registered against the appellants
as well as two others namely Neeraj and Ram Nath.
Mr. S.K. Chaudhary, learned Addl. GA for the State,
submitted that in the murder case of Om Prakash, Case Crime
No. 272 of 2001, police station Laksar, both the appellants were
convicted by the trial court and appeal filed by them being
criminal appeal nos. 188 of 2004 and 189 of 2004 were also
dismissed by this Court vide judgment and order dated
15.12.2010 thereby affirming their conviction and sentence
awarded by the trial court.
Mr. Narayan Har Gupta, learned Amicus Curiae for
the appellants, has vehemently argued that although appellants
in Case Crime No. 272 / 2001 under Section 302, 307 IPC had

5
been convicted, as stated by Mr. S.K. Chaudhary, Addl. GA,
however, appellants cannot be said to be gangsters merely
because they were convicted in the murder case of Om Prakash.
He further submitted that in view of acquittal of two other co-accused by trial court namely Neeraj and Ram Nath, appellants
cannot be said to be members of any Gang, as defined under
Section 2 (b) of the Gangster Act. Section 2 (b) of the Gangster
Act reads as under:
(b) ìGangî means a group of persons, who acting
either singly or collectively, by violence, or threat
or show of violence, or intimidation, or coercion or
otherwise with the object of disturbing public order
or of gaining any undue temporal, pecuniary,
material or other advantage for himself or any
other person, indulge in anti-social activities.
As per definition of Gang, a group of persons acting
either singly or collectively, by violence, or threat or show of
violence, or intimidation or coercion or otherwise with the
object of disturbing public order or of gaining any undue
temporal, pecuniary, material or other advantage for himself or
any other person, indulge in anti-social activities, then that
person acting singly or collectively can be said to be a member
of Gang.
A member or leader or organizer of a gang
including any person, who abets or assists in the activities of a
gang as enumerated in clause (b) shall be a Gangster, as defined
under Section 2 (c) of the Act.
Since both the appellants were held guilty for the
murder of Om Prakash and have criminal antecedents to their

6
credit as shown in the gang-chart, therefore, in my considered
opinion, learned trial court committed no wrong in convicting
the appellants. Moreover, it has not been denied anywhere that
criminal antecedents shown in the gang-chart were, in fact,
never registered against the appellants. Therefore, appeal fails
and is hereby dismissed. If appellants have already served out
the sentence awarded by the trial court, then they shall be
released forthwith, if not wanted in any other case.
Let a copy of this judgment along with lower court
record be sent back to the court below.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
 30.08.2013
SKS
